data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002's claim of EQUAL worst-case vulnerability is asserted but not derived. The mechanism only shows that if services share a causal dependency, a single root cause can fail them all. That establishes a possible shared worst case, not that both architectures have the SAME worst-case vulnerability. A large service with strictly more internal redundancy could have a strictly smaller set of shared critical-path dependencies than a decentralized network, or vice versa; equality of worst-case vulnerability does not follow from the existence of a shared root cause. The counterconditions are all observations, so none supplies the missing covering principle that would make the worst cases equal rather than merely comparable.
